topic: The Geometry of Cramer's Rule: Why Areas Solve Equations
target_audience: Undergraduate students in Linear Algebra or advanced high school students

sections.title: Introduction: The Mixing Robot Mystery
lecture_lines: Meet our robot needing exact fuel amounts.
It must reach a target using two thrusters.
This is a system of linear equations.
animations: Display target vector b = [7, 11] in #00FF00.
Display thruster vectors v1 = [2, 1] in #FF00FF and v2 = [1, 3] in #00FFFF.
Show a robot icon or point at the origin in #FFFFFF.
Animate the equation x*v1 + y*v2 = b appearing in #FFFFFF.
Highlight the unknowns x and y with #FFFF00.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Determinant as Area
lecture_lines: Determinants measure the area of a parallelogram.
Two vectors form the sides of this shape.
If the area is zero, the grid collapses.
animations: Show unit square formed by [1, 0] and [0, 1] in #FFFFFF.
Transform square into parallelogram using v1 and v2 in #00FFFF.
Fill parallelogram interior with #00FFFF and label it det(A).

sections.title: The Linear Combination Visual
lecture_lines: We scale vectors to reach our target point.
Finding x and y means finding these scales.
It's like navigating a custom, skewed grid.
animations: Show vectors v1 and v2 on a coordinate plane in #FF00FF and #00FFFF.
Animate v1 scaling by x and v2 scaling by y to reach b.
Connect scaled vectors tip-to-tail to reach target b in #00FF00.

sections.title: The Geometric Trick: The 'Sliding' Area
lecture_lines: Replace one column with the target vector.
This creates a new, sliding parallelogram area.
Adding a multiple of another vector shears it.
Shearing doesn't change the area's base or height.
So, the new area is x times the original.
animations: Show original parallelogram (v1, v2) in #00FFFF.
Overlay a new parallelogram (b, v2) in #FF00FF.
Express b as x*v1 + y*v2 near the vectors in #FFFFFF.
Show y*v2 part of b 'sliding' along v2 direction, maintaining area.
Highlight that the new area (b, v2) is x * original area (v1, v2).

sections.title: Deriving the Rule: The Ratio of Areas
lecture_lines: The modified area equals x times original area.
Thus, x is the ratio of these areas.
This beautiful ratio is known as Cramer's Rule.
We can find y using the same logic.
Geometry transforms equations into simple ratios.
animations: Display the ratio x = Area(b, v2) / Area(v1, v2) in #FFFFFF.
Show Area(b, v2) as the determinant of matrix A_1 in #FF00FF.
Display the ratio y = Area(v1, b) / Area(v1, v2) in #FFFFFF.
Show Area(v1, b) as the determinant of matrix A_2 in #00FFFF.
Highlight the common denominator det(A) in both formulas in #FFFF00.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Intuition
lecture_lines: Solve equations by comparing geometric areas.
The rule fails if the base area is zero.
Geometry reveals the logic behind the algebra.
animations: Show the robot successfully reaching the target b in #00FF00.
Display det(A) = 0 and show the parallelogram collapsing to a line.
Fade out with the final solved coordinates (x, y) in #FFFFFF.
